definition: Synthetic intelligence (SI) is an alternative/opposite term for artificial intelligence emphasizing that the intelligence of machines need not be an imitation or in any way artificial; it can be a genuine form of intelligence.
details: John Haugeland proposes an analogy with simulated diamonds and synthetic diamonds—only the synthetic diamond is truly a diamond. Synthetic means that which is produced by synthesis, combining parts to form a whole; colloquially, a human-made version of that which has arisen naturally. A "synthetic intelligence" would therefore be or appear human-made, but not a simulation.

explainer.lead: Synthetic intelligence is an alternative term for machine intelligence that stresses it need not imitate or be a lesser copy of human intelligence. It matters as a framing choice about whether machine intelligence is genuine in its own right.

tiers.eli5: A laboratory-grown diamond is still a real diamond — similarly, machine intelligence can be real intelligence, not a fake imitation.
tiers.practitioner: The term is conceptual rather than technical, so engineers rarely use it in code; its practical value is in framing debates, where calling systems 'artificial' versus 'synthetic' shapes how their capabilities are judged.
tiers.paperLevel: There is no formal definition; the argument rests on an analogy in which 'synthetic' means produced by combining parts to form a whole, so a synthetic intelligence is human-made but not a simulation.

explainer.example: Describing a machine reasoner as synthetic intelligence rather than artificial intelligence signals the claim that its reasoning is genuine, not a mere imitation of human thought.
